On MLS®: Chilliwack is a Chilliwack and District Real Estate Board (CADREB) market, not a Fraser Valley or Greater Vancouver board market, and CADREB publishes statistics board-wide only, with no sub-area tables.
A feed count is a snapshot, not a land inventory.

Knight Road is filed on both sides of the Vedder Road divider (Nov 1, 2026). Board data labels Country Park Village (45918 Knight Road) "Sardis East Vedder," while Knight Lodge and Cotton Ridge (45660 / 45645 Knight Road) are labelled "Sardis West Vedder" — the same street on both sides of the divider in board data. A buyer who filters by sub-area label alone will misfile Knight Road product; the address, not the label, governs.
The hillside permit layer is two separate areas, not one. The City's Schedule D separates D-2 Hillside Environment from D-5 Hillside Development as distinct permit areas.

blocks.text: Sardis East / Vedder: streets and boundaries

items.t: Sardis East and Vedder sit on Chilliwack's south side, east of Vedder Road: Sardis is the plan area immediately south of Highway 1, and Vedder (South Vedder) continues south from Sardis to the Chilliwack/Vedder River.

The South Vedder Neighbourhood Plan (OCP Schedule B6, adopted April 2022, updated 2025) puts Vedder Road as South Vedder's western boundary, with the Chilliwack/Vedder River to the south, Promontory to the south-east and Ch'íyáqtel (Tzeachten) First Nation lands to the east.

blocks.text: Sardis East / Vedder: the housing stock

items.t: East Sardis housing clusters around named plan sub-areas in the Sardis Neighbourhood Plan, including Wells Landing, south of Wells Road between the ALR lands and Vedder Road, which the plan describes as a mix of residential uses of varying age and form.

South Vedder's stock mixes older single-family homes along Vedder Road and the river with the newer master-planned streets of Garrison Crossing, where Canada Lands Company refurbished former CFB Chilliwack married quarters and added new townhouses and condominium apartments.

blocks.text: Sardis East / Vedder: rules that affect buyers

items.t: The South Vedder Plan area east of Vedder Road shares a boundary with Tzeachten First Nation along Keith Wilson Road, so lots at the east edge sit beside First Nation lands that the City does not zone.

blocks.text: Sardis East / Vedder: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Sardis Park, a 5-hectare former gravel pit at 6898 School Lane in the park inventory since 1971, has a 655-metre outer looping trail around its pond and hosts the Eco Market on Wednesday nights from May until October.

The Vedder Rotary Loop Trail runs more than 20 kilometres around the Vedder River from Vedder Park, crossing the Vedder Canal on the Keith Wilson Bridge and passing the Great Blue Heron Nature Reserve at kilometre 6.5.
Vedder Park parking lots and trail sections close intermittently for the City's river sediment removal and trail restoration work; the Lickman Road lot was listed closed until November 13, 2026.
The Luckakuck Creek Trail corridor runs through north-east Sardis, and the Sardis Neighbourhood Plan's North Evans sub-area includes a portion of that trail corridor along Evans Road.

Garrison Crossing's Cheamview Crescent loop was deliberately kept at its original PMQ (Permanent Married Quarters) road width, with no curbs, gutters or sidewalks, to preserve how the base streets looked.

blocks.text: Sardis East / Vedder: development and new projects

items.t: 44490 Keith Wilson Road (Garrison/Sardis edge): rezoning application RZ001796, Zoning Bylaw Amendment Bylaw 2026, No. 5530, would amend the CD-16 (Comprehensive Development-16) Zone text to increase density and height and reduce setbacks and parking to facilitate an apartment development. Status: notice of application issued for the March 3, 2026 council meeting (as of November 3, 2026).

South Vedder Neighbourhood Plan implementation: the City's plan for the Vedder Road corridor east of Vedder Road envisions ground-level commercial buildings of 4 storeys, mixed commercial-residential buildings of 6 storeys and standalone residential buildings of 3 to 6 storeys through infill redevelopment along Vedder Road. Status: plan adopted April 2022, updated 2025 (as of November 3, 2026).

blocks.text: Sardis East / Vedder: costs and taxes

items.t: No separate Sardis or Vedder tax rate exists: both neighbourhoods are inside the City of Chilliwack, whose 2050 OCP Schedules B5 and B6 are plan documents, not taxing areas.

blocks.text: Sardis East / Vedder: getting around

items.t: Route 51 Vedder is the main bus spine for this area, running between Downtown Chilliwack and the University of the Fraser Valley Chilliwack campus via Vedder Road, with timing points at Vedder Road at Promontory Road and Vedder Road at Luckakuck Way.
Route 66 Fraser Valley Express stops at Vedder Road at Luckakuck Way, giving east Sardis a direct regional bus to Abbotsford, Langley and Lougheed Town Centre Station.
The Vedder Rotary Loop Trail gives the area a 20-plus-kilometre off-road cycling and walking loop, with parking at Vedder Park, Peach Park, Lickman Road and Hopedale Road.

blocks.text: Sardis East / Vedder: risks and due diligence

items.t: Vedder River sediment is this area's live flood issue: the City states that extreme weather has deposited more sediment in the Vedder River and Canal than typical, raising the river's height and increasing flood risk to the city, which is why it removes sediment in the August–September in-stream works window.

The OCP treats the Sardis–Vedder area as an exception to Chilliwack's floodplain pattern — the plan states that, except for the hillsides and the Sardis–Vedder area, Chilliwack is situated on floodplains — but lots fronting the Vedder River and Luckakuck Creek still need a lot-specific floodplain and riparian (DPA 3) check.
